- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak values by 1–2%.
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤ -0.33), model underestimates; adjust downward bias by +1–1.5% to align with true mean reversion.
- Model often overshoots after sharp sentiment spikes (e.g., sentiment = 1.00 for 3+ days); cap forecast peaks at 1.5–2% below true high observed in 30d window.
- Forecast mean tends to lag true mean by 2–4 days; adjust for mean reversion by adding 0.5–1.0% to forecast if sentiment is neutral or slightly positive.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model overreacts to short-term sentiment; dampen forecast volatility by smoothing 3-day moving average of forecast.
- For 30d horizon, model frequently misses late-period price corrections (last 5–7 days); apply downward bias of 0.5–1.5% to final 5–7 forecast days if sentiment is weak or mixed.
